claims.text: The as-cast or as-solutionized CoCrFeMnNi-based alloy with minor Si/Al additions is single-phase and chemically homogeneous.
Approximately 600–700 °C is near the order–disorder transition temperature of the specified CoCrFeMnNi–Si/Al alloy.
Controlled annealing at 600–700 °C will induce nanoscale phase separation into compositionally distinct precipitates and a matrix.
In situ microstructural monitoring can enable precise control of precipitate formation, size, and distribution.
Keeping particle sizes below the domain-wall width minimizes their pinning effect on domain-wall movement and coercivity.
The compositionally distinct nanoscale precipitates locally enhance magnetic exchange coupling.
The nanoscale precipitates generate beneficial local strain fields.
Precipitate-induced exchange enhancement and strain fields lower the effective energy barrier for magnetization reversal and the critical field for significant magnetization change.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have a higher isothermal magnetic entropy change at low applied fields than the homogeneous baseline.
A fine, uniform precipitate dispersion promotes rapid heat exchange.
A sufficiently fine precipitate dispersion reduces magnetic domain pinning and therefore magnetic hysteresis.
The tailored alloy will show reduced thermal hysteresis relative to the homogeneous baseline.
The optimized precipitate microstructure will maintain or improve mechanical stability relative to the homogeneous baseline.
Annealing outside 600–700 °C or significant composition changes may produce phase behavior that does not support the proposed mechanism.
Precipitate coarsening may compromise mechanical stability.
